title: The geometric operation package
statement:
Over a base scheme $s$, use the coefficient ring $A$, geometric schemes
$a_X:X\to s$ and categories $D(X,A)$ and $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ of [sk-d-setup].
For morphisms $f:X\to Y$ over $s$, use the pro-étale functors of
[sk-def-sf-operations]

$$
f^*,\quad Rf_*,\quad Rf_!,\quad f^!,\quad\otimes_A^{\mathrm L},\quad\RHom_A,
$$

with the adjunctions $f^*\dashv Rf_*$ and $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, the latter whenever
$f$ is compactifiable [def-nagata-compactifiable] and $Rf_!$ has a right
adjoint on the categories in question. In particular the exceptional adjunction
below is on $D^b_{ctf}$; no right adjoint on the whole unbounded pro-étale
derived category is asserted. Here $f^*$ and $f^!$
already denote derived functors; the functors and the two adjunctions are
given, not part of the package. A *geometric operation package* consists of the
coefficient subcategories $D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ of [sk-d-setup] together with
the following data. All operation comparisons are on these subcategories,
with compactifiable morphisms wherever $Rf_!$ or $f^!$ is used; the
monoidal structure on pullback is on $D(-,A)$.

- for every $a_X:X\to s$, a *dualizing complex* $\omega_X\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ for geometric $X$, with
  $\omega_X\simeq a_X^!A$ whenever $a_X$ is compactifiable, a normalization
  $\omega_s\simeq A_s$, and dualizing composition isomorphisms
  $f^!\omega_Y\simeq\omega_X$;
- isomorphisms $Rf_!\simeq Rf_*$ for proper $f$ [def-weil-proper-morphism],
  $Rg_!Rf_!\simeq R(gf)_!$, and $R(\mathrm{id}_X)_!\simeq\mathrm{id}$;
- $!$-base change isomorphisms $g^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!g'^*$ for Cartesian
  squares [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$,
  $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$;
- the projection formula $Rf_!K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}L\simeq Rf_!(K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}f^*L)$,
  natural for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$;
- a strong monoidal structure [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] on every $f^*$, compatible with the braidings of the
  derived categories (these braidings carry the Koszul sign: the braiding of
  $A_X[1]$ with itself is $-1$).

These data satisfy the following coherence conditions, read through the
canonical identity and composition comparisons of the given functors.
The isomorphism $R(\mathrm{id})_!\simeq\mathrm{id}$ satisfies the left and
right unit axioms against $Rg_!Rf_!\simeq R(gf)_!$.
At $f=\mathrm{id}_X$, the proper comparison is
$R(\mathrm{id}_X)_!\simeq\mathrm{id}\simeq R(\mathrm{id}_X)_*$.
The normalization is the composite
$\omega_s\simeq(\mathrm{id}_s)^!A_s\simeq A_s$, the first map being the
specified compactifiable identification of $\omega_s$ and the second the
identity comparison of $(\mathrm{id}_s)^!$ obtained by adjunction from
$R(\mathrm{id}_s)_!\simeq\mathrm{id}$.
The map $(\mathrm{id}_X)^!\omega_X\simeq\omega_X$ is that same adjoint
identity comparison at $\omega_X$, and the monoidal unit map for
$(\mathrm{id}_X)^*$ is the canonical identity pullback comparison.
The proper comparisons and the maps $f^!\omega_Y\simeq\omega_X$ commute
with composition (using the adjoint composition comparison for $f^!$);
$!$-base change commutes with vertical pasting of Cartesian squares. Put

$$
\begin{gathered}
D_XK=\RHom_A(K,\omega_X),\qquad
R\Gamma_c(X,K)=Ra_{X!}K,\qquad
M\boxt N=p_X^*M\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_Y^*N.
\end{gathered}
$$

Here $p_X:X\times_sY\to X$ and $p_Y:X\times_sY\to Y$ are the product
projections. For every complex $K$, evaluation
$D_XK\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}K\to\omega_X$ is the tensor--internal-Hom
adjoint of $\mathrm{id}_{D_XK}$. The biduality map is the adjunct of
$K\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}D_XK\to D_XK\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}K\to\omega_X$,
where the first arrow is the braiding.

Finally, two canonical maps are required to be invertible. *Biduality:* for
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$, the evaluation-adjoint map $K\to D_XD_XK$ is an
isomorphism. *Künneth–Verdier:* if $s$ is the spectrum of a field, then for
$X$, $Y$ quasi-compact and compactifiable over $s$, $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ and
$N\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, the canonical map
$M\boxt D_YN\to\RHom_A(p_Y^*N,p_X^!M)$ on $X\times_sY$, built from the monoidal
structure of $p_Y^*$, the projection formula for $p_X$, $!$-base change, the
identification $\omega_Y\simeq a_Y^!A$ and the counit of $Ra_{Y!}\dashv a_Y^!$,
is an isomorphism. More explicitly, form the trace
$$
\begin{aligned}
t:Rp_{X!}p_Y^*\omega_Y
&\xrightarrow{\sim}a_X^*Ra_{Y!}\omega_Y
\xrightarrow{\sim}a_X^*Ra_{Y!}a_Y^!A_s\\
&\xrightarrow{a_X^*\varepsilon}a_X^*A_s
\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X,
\end{aligned}
$$
where the first arrow is inverse $!$-base change for the product square,
the second uses $\omega_Y\simeq a_Y^!A_s$, and the last is inverse
monoidal unit. The object $p_X^*M\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_Y^*\omega_Y$ lies in
$D^b_{ctf}(X\times_sY,A)$ by stability of $D^b_{ctf}$ under derived pullback
and derived tensor [thm-sf-ctf-stability] (i), (ii), and $A_s\in D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$
(constant, Tor amplitude $[0,0]$), so the exceptional adjunction on $D^b_{ctf}$
applies to the following maps. Let $\alpha_M:p_X^*M\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_Y^*\omega_Y\to p_X^!M$
be the exceptional adjunct of
$$
Rp_{X!}(p_X^*M\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_Y^*\omega_Y)
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{X!}p_Y^*\omega_Y\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M
\xrightarrow{t\otimes1}A_X\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}M\xrightarrow{\sim}M;
$$
the first map uses the braiding and inverse projection formula.
The required Künneth--Verdier map is the tensor--internal-Hom adjunct of
$$
\begin{aligned}
(M\boxt D_YN)\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_Y^*N
&\longrightarrow p_X^*M\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_Y^*(D_YN\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}N)\\
&\xrightarrow{1\otimes p_Y^*\operatorname{ev}_N}
 p_X^*M\otimes_A^{\mathrm L}p_Y^*\omega_Y
\xrightarrow{\alpha_M}p_X^!M,
\end{aligned}
$$
where the first arrow uses associativity and the tensor comparison of
$p_Y^*$; the tensor--Hom adjunction uses the braiding to put $p_Y^*N$
in its prescribed tensor slot.
Coherence always means equality of component morphisms in ordinary categories.

split_report.summary: Definition split only: the current main-20261015 source specifies the geometric operation package as data and coherence axioms, with no proof steps or auxiliary theorem hidden in the definition. I retained its sole blueprint statement dependency sk-d-setup, which fixes the base scheme, geometric schemes, coefficient ring, products, and derived-category setting. The package's functors and adjunctions are explicitly given inputs, while dualizing complexes, compact-support operations, base change, projection, monoidal pullback, biduality, and Kunneth–Verdier invertibility are the fields and required properties of this definition rather than separate proof obligations. The slopmaster2 structure GeometricOperations has the same field-level content but is not an attachment because the prior audit found sorried declarations reachable from it. Second reading adds the existing definition dependencies for the given operations, compactifiability, properness, Cartesian squares and strong monoidal structures; makes the finite-Tor domains explicit; spells out the biduality and Künneth–Verdier arrows; and replaces the ill-typed literal identity shorthand by canonical composites. There are still no proof steps or new nodes.
